items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had met George Kirby in the Philippines the same time as Thad Jones because he was in the same army with Thad and Stanley Facey

ctx.x: So on November 21st of '47, I went into the 845 Club in the Bronx with a small combo lead by Billie Kyle. We were all ex-Sy Oliver members, except Charlie Holmes, the alto sax man. Freddie William was on tenor, George Duvivier on bass and Wallace Bishop on drums. The 845 Club was the only Negro night club in the Bronx

which was not very famous as a night club district but this club did a very good business. The featured, at different times were: Derby Wilson, a fine tap dancer on the Bojangle side, June Richmond who had gone back to her singing act after she left Andy Kirk, Willie Bryant, who was the perm ent Master of Ceremonies, Jackie Mabley, the woman comedian and George Kirby, an imitator of voices. A relief trio was lead by an organist named Lawrence "88" Keys. There was also a chorus line of six girls.

I had met George Kirby in the Philippines the same time as Thad Jones because he was in the same army with Thad and Stanley Facey and had entertained at our recreation hall when I heard Thad playing so much horn. George did an imitation of Joe Louis after he had won a fight and radio announcer would aks Joe to say something to the listeners. Joe had a very southern accent and George imitated him perfectly.
